review_conclusions: Default-off branch preserves the offered palette and existing primitive/execution guards; only already accepted current fine translations receive annotations.

Single-hand visible safe unloaded APPROACH, distance greater than 0.10 m, measured full opening and open command latches are required. Unknown load flags, closed latches, near/contact abstention and current depth veto do not produce the new hint.
At most three distinct accepted fine first paths and one actually robot-path-rejected improving coarse followup are used. No predicted followup is appended to the palette or queued.
Trials bind exact model, limits, action, state q, gripper and commanded latch. Deadlines are checked before and after predicted preflight.
Actor summaries disclose robot-only prediction and lack of future environment authorization. No future q plan or privileged scene truth enters the new actor context.
Independent execution of the complete real gate predicate rejects missing/wrong new flags, wrong source digest, missing task and other guard mismatch; default missing flag remains legacy.
The real runner still selects exactly one currently offered action and rereads actual state before the unchanged servo execution check. No preview execution mechanism was introduced.
limitations: Public open/latch qualification is not an absolute empty-hand or no-environment-contact certificate.
The followup has no future depth observation and is robot-only; no complete swept-scene safety, grasp pose or success claim is warranted.
Saved d075 recomputation reuses already depth-accepted first actions and fixed robot data. It is not a new full scene/controller/actor rollout.
The old H38 subsequently progressed without this feature; no permanent-deadlock or physical success-rate improvement claim.
Neither active/frozen native6f nor the existing H38 source was modified or redeployed. Physical deployment needs a separate prospective authorization.
